claim.markdown_says: `## 15.3.1.5 Permissible values for data associated with ordinal date formats`, `## 15.3.1.6 Week date formats`, `## 15.3.1.7 Permissible values for data associated with week date formats` (all level 2), whereas their siblings on page 829 are `### 15.3.1.1 General`, `### 15.3.1.2 Calendar date formats`, `### 15.3.1.3 ...`, `### 15.3.1.4 Ordinal date formats` (level 3)
claim.why_it_matters: Sibling subsections of the same parent 15.3.1 are transcribed at two different markdown levels. 15.3.1.5, .6 and .7 render as peers of 15.3.1 itself rather than as its children, so a generated section tree loses the parent-child relationship for exactly the subsections that carry the permissible-value ranges for ordinal and week dates.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. The claim is factually accurate about the two texts but describes a markdown formatting artifact, not a content discrepancy, and its own 'missing-heading' label is false. (1) NOTHING IS MISSING. All three headings are present in specs/ISO_COBOL.md with the correct clause number, the correct verbatim title, and a correct anchor: line 33489 ` ## 15.3.1.5 Permissible values for data associated with ordinal date formats`, line 33496 `## 15.3.1.6 Week date formats`, line 33503 `## 15.3.1.7 Permissible values for data associated with week date formats`. The heading levels quoted by the claim are confirmed verbatim (## vs ### on p829: 33443/33458/33465/33474). The claim quotes both sources correctly; the disagreement is over what that difference means. The rendered page image confirms every body paragraph under those three headings is also transcribed completely and accurately (1600/9999 year range, 365/366 day-of-year, the basic/extended week format character counts, the 01-53 vs 01-52 week-of-year rule, the NOTE about January dates falling in the previous year, and the 1-7 Monday-through-Sunday day-of-week rule). (2) THE PDF CARRIES NO HEADING RANK TO LOSE. I rendered both pages at 300 dpi and looked at the printed glyphs. On p829 (printed 799) '15.3.1 Format arguments to international date and time functions', '15.3.1.1 General', '15.3.1.2 Calendar date formats', '15.3.1.3 ...' and '15.3.1.4 Ordinal date formats' are all set in the SAME bold face at the SAME size with the same tab gap after the number. On p830 (printed 800) '15.3.1.5', '15.3.1.6', '15.3.1.7' and '15.3.2 Time formats' are likewise all identical in weight and size. ISO does not typographically distinguish a fourth-level clause head from a third-level one here — depth is encoded ONLY by the dotted number, which the transcription preserves exactly. The claim's own wording concedes this ('all printed at the same rank as 15.3.1.1 through 15.3.1.4'), which means the PDF gives no basis for calling ### right and ## wrong. There is no source distinction that the markdown failed to reproduce. (3) THE 'INCONSISTENT SIBLINGS' FRAMING MISDESCRIBES A DOCUMENT-WIDE PROPERTY. The markdown's hash count is already non-monotonic in this exact region independent of the flagged headings: the PARENT `15.3 Arguments` is `###` (line 33366) while its own child `15.3.1` is `##` (line 33440) — i.e. the parent is transcribed DEEPER than the child. Every 15.3.3.x heading, including the five-level `15.3.3.6.1 Offset subformats` (line 33594), is also `##`. Hash depth in this transcription is not a depth signal anywhere, so 15.3.1.5/.6/.7 are not an anomaly on page 830; they follow the file's prevailing (level-flattened) convention, and it is 15.3.1.1-.4 on page 829 that are the local outlier. (4) NO MEANING CHANGES. Not one word, number, range, or rule differs. Any section-tree generator over this file must key on the dotted clause number (the file's own anchors, `section-15-3-1-5`, already do exactly that); keying on hash count would misparse hundreds of headings across the document regardless of page 830. Rejection criteria fired: the allegedly missing text is present; the difference is purely formatting; the difference does not change meaning. If the hash-depth flattening is to be tracked at all, it belongs as a single document-wide transcription-convention note, not as a per-page structural finding against page 830.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a page-830 content discrepancy. All three headings (15.3.1.5, 15.3.1.6, 15.3.1.7) and all of their body text are transcribed completely and verbatim, with correct clause numbers and correct anchors. The PDF prints 15.3.1, 15.3.1.1 through 15.3.1.7 and 15.3.2 in one identical bold face at one identical size, so it encodes no heading rank for the markdown to lose; depth lives solely in the dotted number, which is preserved. The markdown's hash-level flattening is a document-wide transcription convention — `15.3 Arguments` is itself `###` while its child `15.3.1` is `##`, and all 15.3.3.x headings down to the five-level `15.3.3.6.1` are `##` — so this is at most one global note about heading-depth normalization, not a structural defect on this page.
